pipeline_note: 2026-07-11: design-system/screens/build stages were redefined to produce real, running code (a standalone design-system package + real wired app screens) instead of markdown specs, after user feedback that the prose-based specs produced generic/lossy UI. The design-system, screens, and build stages were reset to pending — their prior 'approved' artifacts (docs/design-system.md, docs/screens.md, the old flat app/ build) do not satisfy the new agent contracts and must be redone. Full review history below is preserved as a record of the OLD pipeline shape. 2026-07-12: the old docs/design-system.md and docs/screens.md were moved to docs/reference/legacy-design-system.md and docs/reference/legacy-screens.md so design-system-architect and screen-designer can still consult them as non-binding reference without those files being silently overwritten/lost when the new agents write their own (much shorter) docs/design-system.md and docs/screens.md. A new user-flow-designer stage was added between sitemap and screens (depends_on sitemap, output docs/user-flows.md) to produce explicit step-by-step flows (error/empty/loading/interruption states) that screen-designer builds against, closing a rigor gap the user flagged. docs/sitemap.md was edited to move Sign Up/Log In from immediately after Splash to immediately before Onboarding Complete (after Profile Setup/Goal Setup/Region Preference/Module Interest/Workout Placement Assessment) per user feedback that onboarding, not account creation, should be the first thing a new user does; sitemap status reset to pending pending re-review of this change. screens now depends_on sitemap, design-system, AND user-flows. 2026-07-12 (later): added a data-research stage (depends_on research-product, output data/) after user feedback that the app must ship with real, cited nutrition and workout-progression data instead of placeholder/mock content. screens and build now also depend_on data-research; screen-designer should use data-research's real content for sample data where available, and app-builder must wire the real data files instead of building its own mock/seeded data layer.

review_log.summary: All four required sections present and accessibility/competitor work is strong, but Pilates (half of workout differentiator #2 in docs/idea.md) is entirely absent, in-workout session execution conventions are missing, and portion-entry conventions for African prepared dishes are unaddressed. See pipeline/review-log.md for the actionable fix list.

All five required sections present; nutrition-side research, market prioritization (Nigeria+Ghana+Kenya), data sourcing, and unified-vs-module recommendation are strong and honest. Rejected because the workout side contradicts docs/idea.md: calisthenics and Pilates appear nowhere, and the bodyweight skill-tree concept is reframed as gym/weights progressive overload (Fitbod/JEFIT competitors, sets/reps/weight requirements). Micronutrient tracking (explicit idea requirement) is missing from Core Feature Requirements, and the idea's open question on validated progression trees is dropped. See pipeline/review-log.md for the actionable fix list.

All four first-pass fixes verified done (Pilates audit via Alo Moves/5 Minute Pilates/NTC, in-workout execution conventions for both modes, household-unit portion-entry note, updated warm/clean-hybrid direction with tonal flex). Rejected because reviewed-and-approved content was silently removed against the explicit preserve-as-is instruction: the gamification quadrant (Duolingo, Habitica) is gone, the named African-brand reference (Flutterwave) was stripped to an unnamed generic, YAZIO was silently swapped for Noom, and the scope note falsely claims those quadrants are 'preserved as reviewed.' Narrow fix list in pipeline/review-log.md; the four new additions are approved as-is and must not change.

All five first-pass fixes verified done: workout module correctly reframed as bodyweight-only calisthenics + Pilates skill tree with objective time-hold/rep-threshold mastery gates and gym/external-load explicitly out of scope; on-category competitors added with sourced complaints (Calistree, Calisthenics Mastery, Thenx, Freeletics as self-rated-gating analogue, Pilatesology/Pilates Anytime); micronutrient tracking is now Core Feature Requirement 4 with named nutrients and FCT-coverage caveats; the progression-tree validation open question is carried forward as explicitly unresolved with an owner type and timing; stale brief-based disclaimer removed. Preservation explicitly verified against the research-design pass-2 failure mode: diaspora persona with dual-cuisine scope-multiplier insight, full Nigeria+Ghana+Kenya priority-markets rationale (shared WAFCT, Kenya FCT 2018, SA/Ethiopia held for v2), and full unified-app-vs-two-modules rationale are all intact at full depth. Sitemap stage unblocked; it must treat progression-tree validation (Open Question 1) as unresolved.

Structure is largely right: 11 of 13 Core Feature Requirements trace fully to real screens, Req 13 is honestly flagged as a cross-cutting engineering constraint, Open Question 1 discipline is correct (placeholder [Skill Node] names, TBD thresholds, no invented progression content), the unified one-app/two-modules structure with shared account/Home/Progress layers is correct, and the three requirement-less screens are all justified. Rejected on two concrete traceability failures: (1) Req 1's portion-photo reference set — which the research calls 'the entry-point that mainstream apps fail' — appears nowhere in the sitemap, yet traceability row 1 claims full coverage without a flag; (2) Req 9's placement assessment is structurally calisthenics-only (singular 'Starting Tier Placement', push/pull/squat-hinge/core-hold steps) with no per-track Pilates placement, reproducing the documented 'I don't know where to start' Pilates-incumbent failure. Narrow two-item fix list in pipeline/review-log.md; everything else is explicitly approved as-is and must not be thinned.

Both first-pass fixes verified done. Fix 1: portion-photo reference now present at three levels — inline on Ingredient Detail alongside the household-unit picker, explicitly included in Composite Meal Detail's portion-selector pattern, and a new Portion Reference Guide sheet/modal (expanded photo set) reachable from both, listed in the modal inventory and navigation summary; traceability row 1 names all three surfaces. Fix 2: placement assessment is now structurally per-track — Assessment Intro states per-track placement up front, a Track Selection step supports one/other/both in either order, separate Calisthenics and Pilates Starting Tier Placement results replace the singular placement, deferral is supported with a re-entry point on Skill Tree Home, and a conditional Combined Assessment Summary covers the both-tracks case; traceability row 9 updated. Open Question 1 discipline held: Pilates placement steps are generic/TBD dimension categories at the same abstraction level as the approved calisthenics patterns, with no invented exercises, orderings, or thresholds. Preservation verified item by item against the first pass's approved-as-is list: five-tab nav, full onboarding sequence, all nutrition screens, the entire workout tier/node/gate set with placeholder discipline, Progress, Profile/Settings, modal inventory, Flags section (Req 13 handling, three justified requirement-less screens), deferred-features list, and the scope note are all intact; every change is additive or the required fix. Screens stage unblocked on the sitemap side (still gated on design-system); carry-forwards for screens recorded in pipeline/review-log.md.

All four pass-2 restoration items verified done: Duolingo and Habitica gamification-audit entries restored with their concrete design lessons (fixed color-semantics mapping; full-game-skin contrast case), the named Flutterwave African-brand entry restored with its design lesson (the diaspora-food-brand paragraph now supplements rather than replaces it), YAZIO restored in the nutrition quadrant (Noom, never-approved intermediate content, correctly dropped per the either/or fix instruction), and the revision note now honestly acknowledges the intermediate pass mistakenly dropped content instead of claiming preservation. All four pass-1 fixes re-verified intact and unchanged per the do-not-touch instruction (Pilates audit with register-contrast takeaway, both in-workout execution subsections with the shared session-player implication, household-unit portion-entry note with sourcing deferred to product research, Recommended Direction confirmed with tonal-flex addendum). Originally-approved content re-verified: full nine-product audit matches the pass-1 recorded list, accessibility section intact with pass-2's approved additive improvements, cultural-identity open question still honestly flagged for the design-system-architect. Agent-spec sections and closing statement present. Design-system stage is unblocked; carry-forwards recorded in pipeline/review-log.md.

Four of five research carry-forwards substantially pass: the session-player tonal flex is correctly one shared component with two presets (missing only the rest-timer state), household-unit portion pickers are the explicit default with the portion-photo reference as a first-class component, the cultural-identity call is resolved explicitly with documented anti-tokenism reasoning (Option 2, restrained), and the accessibility + low-bandwidth/low-end-device rules are comprehensive and structurally honored. Agent-spec output shape is complete (palette, type scale, spacing/grid, component states, accessibility rules). Rejected because carry-forward 1 — the fixed, exclusive gamification color vocabulary — fails on its own terms: SS1.4 claims its colors are 'reserved exclusively for node/skill state,' yet by the doc's own hex tables in-progress = semantic.info, completed = semantic.success, unlocked = brand gold (streak/XP + secondary buttons), and mastered = brand terracotta (every CTA/active tab); SS4.10 then reassigns three of those hexes to macro rings while claiming distinctness from the gamification vocabulary — a factually false internal claim of the kind this pipeline has rejected twice before. Six-item fix list in pipeline/review-log.md (dedicated node-state hexes or honest reasoned scoping, macro-ring fix, rest-timer state, secondary-button color contradiction, non-text 3:1 contrast rule with failing gold-on-light pairings, barcode-deferral alignment with the sitemap); everything else is explicitly approved as-is and must not be thinned.

Five of six first-pass fixes verified done with hexes cross-checked and contrast ratios independently recomputed: (1) all five node states now use genuinely dedicated hexes (locked #8A8578, unlocked #C98A2E, in-progress #3B7EA8, completed #3D8B5C, mastered #A8452A) with zero collisions anywhere in the document and the exclusivity claim now true; (2) SS4.10 honestly documents that macro rings reuse brand/semantic hues while being genuinely distinct from SS1.4; (3) rest-timer state fully specified in SS5.1/SS4.8 with auto-start, timer-xl countdown, 44pt skip/add-time controls, and lock-screen persistence flagged for build; (4) secondary button has one owner (terracotta-outlined) in both SS1.1 and SS4.1; (6) barcode explicitly deferred per the approved sitemap. Preservation verified item by item — nothing thinned. Rejected narrowly because fix 5 was only half-applied and fix 1 introduced a knock-on contrast failure: gold-muted #E0BE7C — named by hex in the pass-1 fix list — is still the Pilates player's sole progress indicator at ~1.6:1 against its light surface (~1.0:1 against the standard track), directly contradicting the new SS6.10 rule (3:1 for progress fills), which bans base gold but is silent on gold-muted; and the new node.unlocked amber #C98A2E computes to ~2.7:1 on the app background (~2.4:1 on cards), below SS6.10's own 3:1 minimum for node-state fills (the other four node hexes pass). Two-item mechanical fix list in pipeline/review-log.md; all six fix areas where marked done, and everything previously approved, must be preserved as-is.

Both pass-2 fixes verified done, with every stated contrast figure independently recomputed via the WCAG relative-luminance formula and confirmed accurate: node.unlocked is now #A85F12 (4.41:1 vs app background #F7F3EE, 3.93:1 vs card #EDE6DC — matching the doc's claims; additionally verified 3.65:1/3.19:1 on the dark surfaces where SS5.1 permits node colors), and gold-muted is now #7A4E12 (6.50:1 vs background, 5.79:1 vs card, 3.99:1 vs the warmgray-400 track — matching the doc's claims; the old ~1.6:1/~1.0:1 failure is documented honestly and the old hex banned). Full-palette hex-exclusivity re-verified from scratch: #A85F12 and #7A4E12 collide with nothing (brand, semantic, neutrals, other node states, macro rings), and SS1.4's dedication claim remains true. Design coherence: no new near-duplicate — gold-muted vs node.unlocked are luminance-distinct with disjoint contexts; node.unlocked vs gold-dark is the closest pair (an inevitable consequence of the pass-2 darkening instruction), non-blocking with a screens-stage carry-forward. The two additive notes check out: SS1.4's locked-state WCAG 1.4.11 inactive-component exemption is correctly reasoned with an explicit invalidation condition, and SS4.7 now names color.node.unlocked per the optional fix. Preservation verified section by section — SS0, SS2, SS3, SS4.3/4.4, SS5 structure, SS6 rules 1-9, neutrals/dark-mode all unchanged; every change traces to the fix list. Non-blocking observations recorded (mastered ~3.0:1/~2.6:1 on dark surfaces with a compliant outline/icon path, SS6.4's 2.5.4-vs-2.3.1 citation, gold-muted naming). Screens stage now fully unblocked (both dependencies approved); seven carry-forwards recorded in pipeline/review-log.md, and the orchestrator should consider running the screens merge-point review at effort xhigh.

Merge-point review (depends on both sitemap and design-system, checked independently at high rigor). Against sitemap: every screen in the sitemap's list maps to a section (onboarding A1-A8 incl. all five placement sub-screens A7a-A7g, Home, Nutrition N1-N13, Workout W1-W8, Progress P1-P3, Profile/Settings S1-S8, all six modals). Per-track placement flow fully represented (A7b Track Selection -> A7c/d Calisthenics and/or A7e/f Pilates in either order -> A7g optional Combined Summary -> W1 deferred re-entry). Portion-photo reference (SS4.4) present on Ingredient Detail (N4), Composite Meal Detail (N5), and Portion Reference Guide (N6). Against design-system: only approved tokens/hexes used; unlocked = #A85F12, Pilates progress = gold-muted #7A4E12; superseded #C98A2E/#E0BE7C appear only in never-used disclaimers. Locked nodes documented fully non-interactive (W2/W3), preserving the WCAG 1.4.11 inactive-component exemption. Combined Progress Dashboard (P1) separates carbs ring (#A9761E) and unlocked-node indicator (#A85F12) into distinct titled sections, each carrying its required icon/label pairing. Dark-mode node maps render on dark-bg #17181A with mastered outline/icon (not fill #A8452A) as primary contrast signal. Honesty verified: the five flagged missing components (segmented control, single-select, toggle/switch, calendar/date-picker, trend chart) are genuinely absent from design-system SS4 and genuinely required; the guided Session Player scope mismatch is accurate (sitemap has no player destination, W7 stays freeform-logging-only, no player screen invented). Discipline verified: no invented exercise names, thresholds, or node orderings; [Skill Node] and TBD preserved throughout. Non-blocking observations only (expandable/accordion used in A4/N5/S8 without a formal component flag; A7g names calisthenics accent but not Pilates; A1 splash uses type.display). Build carry-forward: build W7 freeform logging only; do NOT build a guided Session Player screen (SS4.8/SS5 component is deferred until a sitemap destination exists); implement the five flagged components as additive to the design system.

Final-stage review; the entire app/src tree was read file-by-file against docs/screens.md, docs/sitemap.md, docs/design-system.md, and the four build carry-forwards. Most of the build verifies faithful: five-tab shell and every sitemap screen/route present (N3 rendered inline in N2 and N4/N5 merged into one FoodDetailScreen, both documented); per-track placement flow with deferral and Skill Tree Home re-entry implemented; tokens.ts transcribes the approved palette 1:1 with node.unlocked #A85F12 and gold-muted #7A4E12, and the superseded #C98A2E/#E0BE7C appear nowhere in app/src; skill-tree/placement content is genuinely placeholder-only ('Skill Node A', TBD thresholds, generic form cues); foodDatabase.ts is prominently labeled mock with an in-app caveat; no guided Session Player was built (W7 is freeform-only per the screens adjudication); locked nodes are hard-guarded non-interactive in SkillNode.tsx; node maps force dark-bg with mastered outline/icon as the contrast signal; the five flagged components plus list-row were built additively; and nearly every BUILD_NOTES claim spot-checked true against source. Rejected on four concrete failures: (1) gold-muted #7A4E12 is used as a decorative portion-tile background fill (Waakye tone in foodDatabase.ts, rendered as backgroundColor by PortionPhotoReference) — violating the design system's progress-fill-only restriction — while BUILD_NOTES falsely claims the token is 'reserved-but-unused', the exact false-internal-claim pattern this pipeline has rejected twice; semantic success/warning hexes are also used as decorative tile tones; (2) node-state chips on Node Detail (W3) and Progression Status (W6) render node states in semantic StatusBadge colors (mastered = semantic.warning orange) instead of the SS1.4 node colors the screens doc explicitly requires; (3) custom foods (N7/Req 2) are save-only dead data — nothing reads state.customFoods, so a created food can never be searched or logged, 'Save & log now' does not route to Confirm & Log, and the cut is undocumented; (4) Combined Summary's 'Adjust a placement' navigates to PlacementResult with fabricated params whose mount effect silently overwrites the calisthenics starting tier to 3. Four minor fix-alongside items: P1's carbs and unlocked-node indicators are bare colored dots contra carry-forward #6, W2 shows no prerequisite edges/captions (silent deviation), Weight Log deletes entries on a bare tap with no confirm, and FoodDetailScreen has a Rules-of-Hooks hazard (early return above useMemo). Verification limitation recorded: the reviewer session had no shell, so the builder's tsc/expo-export claims could not be independently re-run — the revision must include fresh tsc output or the orchestrator should re-run it. Nine-item fix list in pipeline/review-log.md; everything under 'What passes' is explicitly approved as-is and must not be thinned.

All nine first-pass fixes verified genuinely made by reading the source directly, not BUILD_NOTES: (1) tile tones in foodDatabase.ts now use only SS1.1 brand hues (#A9761E/#C1502E/#1F5C42/#D9A441/#96391F) — #7A4E12 and the semantic hexes are gone from tones, PortionPhotoReference documents the tone restriction, and BUILD_NOTES' goldMuted claim is now true (sole occurrence is its tokens.ts definition) with the prior falsehood explicitly acknowledged; (2) new NodeStateBadge renders SS1.4 node color + icon + label from the NODE_STATE_META mapping exported by SkillNode itself, used in W3 and W6 — StatusBadge no longer touches node state and the dead STATE_TONE copy is removed; (3) custom foods traced functional end-to-end: customFoodToFoodItem/findFood/searchAllFoods helpers, state.customFoods merged into all four Add Entry tabs, FoodDetail and ConfirmLog resolve custom ids, ADD_RECENT round-trips, and 'Save & log now' saves then routes to Confirm & Log with a real 1x portion; (4) 'Adjust a placement' fixed with per-track buttons + review mode — PlacementResult in review never computes or dispatches SET_PLACEMENT (effect early-returns) and displays the stored tier; the only mutation path is explicit Retake through a fresh non-review mount (stack ordering traced); (5) P1 indicators now carry ellipse-outline/#A85F12 and pie-chart-outline/carbs glyphs — no bare dots; (6) W2 locked nodes show static 'Requires:' prerequisite captions (caption-only option, documented); (7) Weight Log delete requires an explicit confirm card matching N9/S2; (8) FoodDetailScreen hooks all run before the not-found early return; (9) tsc claim verified via the orchestrator's independent run (exit 0 before and after) — this reviewer session again had no shell, disclosed honestly. Preservation re-verified across every touched file plus navigators, tokens.ts, skillTree.ts, and state layer: no superseded hexes, no player route, locked-node guard and placeholder discipline intact, offline machinery untouched, nothing thinned. Three non-blocking polish items recorded (PortionReferenceGuide and FavoritesRecents still resolve seed ids only — blank modal / omitted listing for custom foods; PlacementSteps retains local state across a same-session cross-track retake). FINAL GATE PASSED — the pipeline is complete.

Re-review after the auth reorder (Sign Up/Log In moved from immediately after Splash to immediately before Onboarding Complete). Change isolation verified independently via git diff against the pass-2-approved commit: exactly three changes (the moved bullet with rationale and returning-user short-circuit, the rewritten section-2 pre-nav line, and the new pre-auth-state flag) — nothing else touched, nothing thinned. Internal consistency holds: section-1 order matches the section-2 nav summary exactly, the old 'Splash -> Auth' label is fully replaced with no dangling reference (grep-verified), traceability row 12 is order-agnostic and still true, and the new flag names exactly the five now-pre-auth screens and delegates to user-flow-designer, which exists in state.json. Traceability to research-product unaffected: no requirement mandates auth-first; Req 12 still satisfied (account precedes the tab bar, so all in-app data stays account-tied); Req 9's pre-account placement results are exactly what the new flag covers; Req 5 offline-first is reinforced. Three non-blocking flow-level carry-forwards recorded for user-flow-designer: returning-user landing (Welcome vs. straight to tabs), whether Sign Up is a hard wall (a guest/skip mode would contradict Req 12 and must return to sitemap), and log-in-with-partial-local-onboarding-state conflict resolution. user-flows unblocked on the sitemap side; pass-2 carry-forwards remain in force.

Coverage and carry-forward resolution are genuinely strong: every sitemap screen and all six modals trace to a flow with systematic error/empty/loading/interruption states via six well-factored common patterns; all three sitemap-re-review carry-forwards are resolved explicitly in Section 0 (pre-auth draft recovery + field-level server-wins merge for the login-with-unsynced-draft conflict, returning-user lands straight on Home, Sign Up hard wall tied to Req 12 with the change-is-sitemap-level note); all four fork/join points (Module Interest, per-track placement with deferral, draft-attach at Sign Up with an atomicity default, deferred-placement re-entry) are explicit; 15 reasoned defaults honestly consolidated in Section G. Rejected on four narrow items: (1) an internal routing contradiction on the returning-user short-circuit - A1 routes the no-session-no-draft precondition to Profile Setup while A7b step 1 and E2 step 4 route the identical precondition straight to Sign Up/Log In, and the short-circuit's actual trigger/affordance is never specified, in exactly carry-forward #2's area; (2) a fabricated verbatim sitemap quote in A3 ('If only one track was chosen, this step is skipped' appears nowhere in docs/sitemap.md - grep-verified); (3) 'per the sitemap's per-step actions' cited for a Skip-this-step behavior the sitemap never defines; (4) cached-session Splash-to-Home routing in 0.2/A7a mis-cited 'per the sitemap', which never mentions cached sessions. Items 2-4 are the false-internal-claim pattern this pipeline has rejected three times before; the underlying behaviors are fine and need relabeling as reasoned defaults, not redesign. Everything under 'What passes' is approved as-is and must not be thinned. Fix list in pipeline/review-log.md.

Independently verified: both JSONs parse, all 73 skill thresholds carry confidence tags, prerequisite graph fully resolves, no [Skill Node]/TBD placeholders, and 10+ spot-checked figures are genuinely accurate (all 8 USDA rows exact vs FoodData Central incl. portion grams; nyama choma matches USDA roasted goat; garri/jollof/akara/moin-moin Atwater-consistent; ogbono's documented 250g-to-100g derivation computes). Regional coverage (Nigeria 10/Ghana 5/Kenya 9/Diaspora 8), swallow-style household-unit portions, real CC-ordered calisthenics lines, convergent muscle-up/pistol/handstand gates, canonical classical-Pilates tiering, and the headline honesty claims (no-direct-FCT-access disclosed in-file; banku/terere/suya/groundnut gaps genuinely null/flagged in the data, not glossed) all pass. Rejected on five concrete items: (1) egusi contradicts its own valueSpread (182 kcal/100g x 250g ladle = 455 kcal vs the 350-400/serving range it cites as 'consistent'); (2) mandazi portion math contradicts its own valueSpread (60g piece x 320/100g = 192 kcal/piece vs claimed 292-320/piece; plus a physically implausible 28 kcal/piece mahamri aside); (3) Req-4 micronutrient coverage fails traceably and undisclosed - B12 appears in ZERO of 32 foods (the sitemap's B12 trend screen can never show data), zinc 1/vitA 2/folate 1, only 11 of 32 foods have any non-null micronutrient, and the 8 USDA items have near-empty panels despite the cited source publishing full panels for exactly those foods - an omission the limitations section never states; (4) gh-waakye and gh-fufu carry the compiled-estimate label without the range/reason valueSpread the file's own legend defines that label as requiring; (5) skill-tree 'medium' confidence claims thresholds sourced to Convict Conditioning but the volumes are not CC's published standards (CC wall push-up progression standard is 3x50 vs 2x20 here) - disclosed only on the push line, silently overclaimed on pull/squat/core. Items 1-2 violate the agent spec's own step 4 (conversions must compute, no silent self-contradictions); item 5 is the recurring claimed-provenance pattern. Narrow fix list in pipeline/review-log.md; everything under 'What passes' is approved as-is and must not be thinned (in particular, honest nulls must not be deleted to improve item 3's counts).
